title: See a performance inside the Sydney Opera House
description: Utzon's World Heritage shells are worth seeing from the inside - the Concert Hall reopened in 2022 after a major acoustic rebuild.

title: Climb the arch of the Sydney Harbour Bridge
description: 134m above the water on the arch of the Coathanger. The pedestrian walkway underneath is free if the climb price stings.

title: Walk to Mrs Macquarie's Chair through the Royal Botanic Garden
description: Free harbourside gardens on Gadigal land since 1816, ending at the sandstone bench with the classic Opera House and Bridge view.

title: Drink in the oldest pubs in The Rocks
description: Convict-era sandstone lanes under the bridge, with a weekend market and several pubs each claiming to be Sydney's oldest.

title: Walk the sandstone headland at Barangaroo Reserve
description: A container terminal rebuilt into a naturalistic headland from 10,000 hand-cut sandstone blocks, named for a Cammeraygal woman.

title: Swim between the flags at Bondi Beach
description: Australia's most famous kilometre of sand, and the birthplace of the surf lifesaving movement.

title: Walk the whole Bondi to Coogee coastal path
description: 6km of clifftop path past five beaches and the Waverley Cemetery - do it in October when Sculpture by the Sea takes over.

title: Swim a lap at Bondi Icebergs while waves break over the wall
description: An ocean pool at the south end of Bondi, open since 1929, where the surf washes straight into the lane you are swimming.

title: Ride the ferry and the cable car into Taronga Zoo
description: A zoo on a harbour hillside where the giraffes have a better view of the Opera House than most hotels.

title: Catch the Manly ferry across Sydney Harbour
description: Thirty minutes from Circular Quay for the price of a bus ticket - the best-value harbour cruise in the world.

title: Hike the Manly to Spit Bridge track
description: 10km through harbourside bush, Aboriginal rock engravings and hidden beaches most Sydneysiders have never walked.

title: Watch the Saturday night fireworks over Darling Harbour
description: A reclaimed goods harbour turned promenade of museums, aquarium and restaurants around the water.

title: Explore the Naala Badu building at the Art Gallery of NSW
description: Free entry, and since 2022 a second building including the Tank - a WWII naval oil bunker turned vast underground gallery.

title: Meet the megafauna at the Australian Museum
description: The country's first museum, opened 1827, with dinosaur and First Nations galleries and free general entry.

title: Spend a weekend in the Blue Mountains
description: A World Heritage sandstone plateau split by huge valleys, blue with eucalyptus haze, ninety minutes by train from Sydney.

title: See the Three Sisters lit up after dark at Echo Point
description: Three sandstone pinnacles above the Jamison Valley, central to Gundungurra and Darug stories, floodlit each evening.

title: Ride the steepest passenger railway in the world at Scenic World
description: A 52-degree incline railway built to haul coal, plus a glass-floored cableway over the Jamison Valley.

title: Walk the National Pass at Wentworth Falls
description: A track cut into the cliff face by hand in 1908, running along a ledge halfway down a 187m waterfall.

title: Descend into the Grand Canyon Track at Blackheath
description: A 6km loop into a narrow fern-hung sandstone slot canyon - cool and dripping even in February.

title: Go through the Lucas Cave at Jenolan
description: Among the oldest discovered open cave systems on earth, dated at around 340 million years. Check access - the road has closed for repairs at times.

title: Eat at the art deco Paragon in Katoomba
description: The mountains' main town, full of 1930s guesthouses and cafes, and the base for every walk on the escarpment.

title: Canoe the Kangaroo River through Kangaroo Valley
description: A green valley enclosed by escarpment, with wombats on the flats and a river gentle enough to paddle all day.

title: Watch dolphins from a boat in Jervis Bay
description: A huge sheltered bay with a resident bottlenose dolphin population, and humpbacks passing through in winter and spring.

title: Walk the famously white sand at Hyams Beach
description: Long claimed as the whitest sand in the world - go outside January, when the village is genuinely overwhelmed.

title: Snorkel Green Patch in Booderee National Park
description: A national park owned and jointly managed by the Wreck Bay Aboriginal Community, with the clearest water on the South Coast.

title: Get soaked by the Kiama Blowhole on a big southeast swell
description: A sea cave that fires spray up to 25m into the air - it only really performs when the swell comes from the southeast.

title: Cross the Hampden Bridge at Kangaroo Valley
description: An 1898 sandstone-turreted suspension bridge, the oldest of its kind still standing in Australia.

title: Walk part of the Coast Track in the Royal National Park
description: The world's second-oldest national park, gazetted in 1879 - a 26km coast track of heath, cliffs and empty beaches.

title: Time the tide right for the Figure Eight Pools
description: Rock pools eroded into figure-eights on a wave-swept shelf. People are seriously injured here regularly - only go on a low tide with a small swell, and check the NPWS risk rating first.

title: Jump into the lagoon at Wattamolla
description: A waterfall dropping into a saltwater lagoon behind a beach, in the middle of the Royal National Park.

title: Watch the hang gliders launch at Bald Hill above Wollongong
description: An escarpment city between mountains and sea, with one of Australia's great paragliding launch sites at Stanwell Park.

title: Drive the Sea Cliff Bridge out over the ocean
description: A 665m curved bridge built out over the water after rockfalls closed the cliff road - park and walk the pedestrian lane.

title: Taste aged Semillon in the Hunter Valley
description: Australia's oldest wine region, and the only place making Hunter Semillon - a style that starts thin and becomes extraordinary after a decade.

title: See the Christmas lights at Hunter Valley Gardens
description: Ten themed gardens over 25 hectares, which turn into one of the largest Christmas light displays in the country.

title: Sandboard the Stockton dunes at Port Stephens
description: The largest moving coastal sand dunes in the Southern Hemisphere, 32km long, with camel trains and toboggans on them.

title: Go dolphin watching out of Nelson Bay
description: Around 100 bottlenose dolphins live in Port Stephens year-round, which makes the boat trips unusually reliable.

title: Climb Tomaree Head for the summit view
description: A short steep climb up a 161m volcanic headland with WWII gun emplacements and a view down the whole coastline.

title: Swim at Wategos and watch the sunrise crowd at Byron Bay
description: The most easterly town on the mainland - surf breaks, a hinterland of rainforest, and no longer remotely a secret.

title: Stand on the most easterly point of mainland Australia
description: A 3.7km loop up to the 1901 lighthouse, past the marker for the continent's easternmost point, with whales offshore mid-year.

title: Fish off the breakwater at Brunswick Heads
description: The quieter, cheaper, friendlier town fifteen minutes north of Byron, on a river mouth with a good pub and a good pie.

title: Walk the Wonga Walk through Dorrigo rainforest
description: Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage - a 6.6km loop under strangler figs and past two waterfalls you walk behind.

title: Stand on the Dorrigo Skywalk above the canopy
description: A boardwalk projecting out over the escarpment so you look across the top of the rainforest to the coast 60km away.

title: Climb the Big Banana at Coffs Harbour
description: Built in 1964 and the original Australian Big Thing, now with a waterpark and toboggan run attached.

title: Dive the Solitary Islands Marine Park
description: Where tropical and temperate currents collide - grey nurse sharks, turtles and coral at a latitude that should not have any.

title: Walk the Bathers Way from Nobbys to Merewether
description: A steel city that reinvented itself - 6km of coastal path linking four ocean baths, a fort and a working coal harbour.

title: Swim in the restored Newcastle Ocean Baths
description: A 1922 art deco seawater pool with its famous painted pavilion, reopened after a long restoration.

title: Walk the painted breakwall at Port Macquarie
description: Thousands of individually painted rocks along the breakwall, added by visitors for decades - find a blank one and add yours.

title: Meet the patients at the Port Macquarie Koala Hospital
description: The world's first hospital dedicated to koalas, running since 1973 - free entry, donation-funded, daily feed walks.

title: Climb Mount Gower on Lord Howe Island
description: World Heritage, capped at 400 visitors at a time. The Mount Gower climb is a guided 875m ascent rated among the best day walks on earth.

title: See the summer wildflowers in Kosciuszko National Park
description: Australia's alpine heart - snow gums, glacial lakes and a brief, spectacular wildflower season above the treeline.

title: Stand on the highest point in Australia
description: 2,228m, and unusually approachable - the chairlift from Thredbo puts you within a 13km return walk on a metal mesh path.

title: Ski Thredbo, the longest run in Australia
description: 672m vertical and a 5.9km top-to-bottom run - the most serious ski terrain in the country, and a downhill bike park in summer.

title: Drive the Alpine Way through the Snowy Mountains
description: A mountain road from Jindabyne to Khancoban past the Snowy Hydro scheme, one of the great engineering projects of the 20th century.

title: Stand where the oldest known cremation on earth took place at Mungo
description: A dry lake bed on Barkandji, Mutthi Mutthi and Ngiyampaa country, where Mungo Lady and Mungo Man show 40,000+ years of continuous culture.

title: Walk the Walls of China at sunset
description: A 33km crescent of eroded sand and clay lunettes that glows orange at last light. Access is by guided tour to protect the fossil beds.

title: See the light at Broken Hill, Australia's first heritage-listed city
description: A silver mining town in the far west that became an artists' colony - Pro Hart, the Palace Hotel and a mullock heap over the main street.

title: Watch the sun set through the Living Desert Sculptures
description: Twelve sandstone sculptures carved in situ on a hilltop outside Broken Hill by artists from around the world in 1993.

title: Fossick for black opal at Lightning Ridge
description: The only significant source of black opal on earth, plus free artesian bore baths at 41 degrees and some deeply eccentric buildings.

title: Sleep beside the lions at Dubbo
description: The regional centre of the central west, best known as the base for the open range zoo just outside town.

title: Cycle the 5km circuit at Taronga Western Plains Zoo
description: An open range zoo you tour by bike or cart, with black rhino, giraffe and one of the world's most successful breeding programs.

title: Watch Fitzroy Falls drop off the escarpment
description: An 81m single-drop waterfall over the Illawarra escarpment, in cool-climate country of Bowral, Berrima and Robertson.

title: Get properly remote in Wollemi National Park
description: The largest wilderness in NSW, and where the Wollemi pine - a species thought extinct for two million years - was found in 1994.

title: Switch your torch off in the Glow Worm Tunnel
description: An abandoned 400m railway tunnel near Newnes, now curved, pitch dark and covered in glow worms.

title: Find the ruins of the Newnes shale oil works
description: A ghost industrial site in the Wolgan Valley - brick kilns and retorts from a 1900s shale oil town, slowly going back to bush.

title: Stargaze in Warrumbungle, Australia's only Dark Sky Park
description: Volcanic spires including the Breadknife, and Australia's first International Dark Sky Park, next to Siding Spring Observatory.
